documents.unit: Center for Teaching Excellence (approved by Office of Academic Affairs)
documents.title: Syllabus Statements to Address the Usage of Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university rule. It offers three Academic Affairs-approved sample statements ('EMBRACE/PERMIT', 'LIMITED/SELECT USAGE', 'PROHIBIT/EXCLUDE') for 'instructors who choose', so the decision is left to instructors and tiers are listed.
documents.summary: A Center for Teaching Excellence page gives faculty three sample syllabus statements approved by Academic Affairs: permit with citation, limited use on select assignments, and prohibit. Faculty are encouraged to adopt one and share their own language; the university sets no default.

units.why: The page tells faculty they are 'encouraged to add one of the three sample statements' to syllabi; this asks instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus, so P09, though it is encouragement rather than a requirement.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to add one of the three sample statements below to their syllabi
units.frag_end: Office of Academic Affairs has approved.
units.fit_note: The statement is encouraged, not required; it is not mandatory in every syllabus.

units.why: The page offers three sample statements headed 'EMBRACE/PERMIT', 'LIMITED/SELECT USAGE' and 'PROHIBIT/EXCLUDE', which are named levels of AI use that instructors choose among, so P05 (tiers) rather than P04.
units.frag_end: Office of Academic Affairs has approved.
units.policy: The university offers three approved sample syllabus statements: embrace/permit, limited/select usage, and prohibit/exclude.

units.why: Each statement is for 'instructors who choose' it and the statements are only 'suggested'; no university-wide default is set and the choice is left to instructors, so P04.
units.policy: Instructors choose which of the suggested sample AI statements, if any, applies in their course.

units.why: Faculty are invited to share their own AI syllabus statements and assignment language with the CTE to 'build a repository'. This is closest to P63 (support for faculty) although it is about contributing, not learning.
units.anchor: faculty are invited to share their AI-related syllabus statements
units.fit_note: Covers instructors sharing their statements to build a campus repository, not workshops or advice on learning AI.

units.why: The permit statement says AI 'may be used for any assignment', a default of permission for all work, so P02.
units.anchor: may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation
units.frag_end: fact-checking statements composed by AI Generative Software.
units.policy: AI language models such as ChatGPT may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation.

units.why: The same sentence conditions permission on 'appropriate citation', a disclosure requirement attached to each use, so P24. It is a separate rule from the permission itself.
units.policy: AI use must be accompanied by appropriate citation.

units.why: Students are told they are 'responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI'; AI output may be wrong and the student must verify it, so P31 rather than P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI Generative Software.

units.why: The permit statement opens with a rationale that ChatGPT 'enhanc[es] both teaching and learning'; this welcomes AI as an educational benefit, closest to P44 though it is not about professional skill.
units.anchor: offers an innovative and effective approach to education
units.fit_note: Frames AI as beneficial to teaching and learning generally, not as a professional skill employers expect.

units.why: The limited statement says ChatGPT 'should be used selectively and thoughtfully', a limit on AI use that stops short of a ban, so P04/P03 are both close. I chose P03 because the sentence advises restraint; the per-assignment choice is coded in the next unit.
units.anchor: it should be used selectively and thoughtfully
units.fit_note: Selective use is recommended as permitted in limited form; it is not framed as discouraging AI.

units.why: The statement says AI 'may be used on select assignments in this course, as defined by the instructor'; permission is per assignment and set by the instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: may be used on select assignments in this course, as defined by the instructor

units.why: The statement says limited usage keeps ChatGPT 'a supplementary tool rather than a replacement for human interaction'. No type covers keeping AI secondary to human interaction, and P32 is about the student as problem-solver, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: serves as a supplementary tool rather than a replacement for human interaction
units.uncovered_note: AI should supplement and not replace human interaction in teaching and learning.

units.why: Students who are unsure whether use is appropriate are told 'please see me for guidance', which is asking the instructor first, so P10.
units.frag_start: If you are unsure as to

units.why: The limited statement repeats the duty to fact-check AI-composed statements. It is a separate sample statement, so it is coded again as P31.
units.anchor: You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI Generative Software.

units.why: The prohibit statement says 'use of ChatGPT in this course is prohibited', a ban on AI for the course, so P01.
units.anchor: The use of ChatGPT in this course is prohibited
units.frag_start: The use of ChatGPT in this course
units.policy: The use of ChatGPT in this course is prohibited.

units.why: The ban is justified by 'concerns regarding its potential impact on the quality of education and the development of crucial skills'; the reason is protecting skill development, so P41.
units.anchor: potential impact on the quality of education and the development of crucial skills
units.frag_start: The use of ChatGPT in this course

units.why: Students are told 'All work submitted in this course must be your own', which is ownership of submissions, so P29.
units.anchor: All work submitted in this course must be your own
units.frag_start: All work submitted in this course

units.why: The statement ties the work to the University's 'Administrative Guidelines on Academic Integrity', placing AI use under existing integrity rules (P36), though it names no process or penalty.
units.frag_start: All work submitted in this course
units.policy: Work submitted must be completed per the University's Administrative Guidelines on Academic Integrity.
units.fit_note: Refers to existing integrity guidelines without naming AI misuse as misconduct explicitly.

units.why: The text forbids 'unauthorized collaboration or use [of] ChatGPT or other AI composition software'; use needs authorization, which works as a permission-required fallback, so P06 rather than P01 (already coded above).
units.anchor: You may not engage in unauthorized collaboration or use ChatGPT or other AI composition software.
units.fit_note: Bans use and unauthorized collaboration together; the fallback is that the instructor's permission is required.

units.why: The last sentence says 'Using these tools without my permission puts your academic integrity at risk', treating unauthorized AI use as an integrity matter, so P36.
units.anchor: Using these tools without my permission puts your academic integrity at risk.
units.fit_note: Warns of integrity risk but names no process or penalty.

notes: Single short page with three sample statements; no school or computing policy found. The fact-checking sentence appears in two different sample statements, so it is coded twice.
